study type: Retrospective population-based cohort study with a matched cohort analysis
cohort: The study cohort consisted of pregnant women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), divided into those who conceived via IVF and those who conceived naturally, using data from the Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project Nationwide Inpatient Sample (2004-2014).
finding: Among pregnant women with PCOS, IVF was associated with an increased risk for preterm delivery and, in the matched cohort, a higher risk of placental abnormalities including placenta previa and placental abruption.
mod_finding: IVF was associated with a higher risk of operative vaginal delivery and cesarean section in singleton pregnancies.
